sasha: quick question about generation edge cases — I'm seeing some surprising behavior when a stop sequence and max_tokens both apply. is the runtime guaranteed to cut at the first stop even if that would exceed max_tokens, or does max_tokens always win?

alex: quick answer: max_tokens always caps generations. stop sequences cause truncation earlier only if they occur within the token limit. so you won't get > max_tokens. saw this in the sampler tests. :white_check_mark:

maria: here's the API contract snippet we keep in the docs (paraphrased): "max_tokens sets a hard upper bound on the number of tokens emitted by the model. stop sequences are applied to the emitted stream and may truncate before max_tokens is reached; they do not extend the limit."

jon: that matches my integration tests, but edge case: when stop matches mid-token (byte-level thing), do we return partial token or always only whole tokens?

alex: model runs at token granularity; we never return half tokens in the response. if stop aligns inside a token by string match, the matching is done on decoded text, so we may cut the decoded string and then drop the last partial token from tokenized numeric output — practically you see the truncated text and token_count <= max_tokens.

sasha: thanks. second question: logprobs + stop. if the response is truncated by a stop sequence, do the returned logprobs include the stop token probability or not?

maria: short: only for tokens that are actually emitted. we don't synthesize a special "stop token" logprob unless the model emitted that token literally. for some decoders we have an internal end-of-sequence marker, but it's not always surfaced. tests: logprobs array length == tokens array length.

priyanka: note for the rollout — we changed one internal sampler behavior last week (PR #3245) where we normalized the top_p distribution after temperature scaling. that fixed some degeneracies but might change logprob distributions slightly. @alex can confirm the perf tests?

alex: confirmed. normalization after temperature scaling means when temp>0 we apply softmax( logits / temp ), then do nucleus truncation on cumulative prob mass, then renormalize. Previous behavior truncated then applied temperature which produced odd artifacts. The change is semantically different but consistent with most academic implementations. perf/bandwidth unchanged.

jon: was that backwards-compatible? some customers rely on sticky deterministic samplers when temp=0 and top_p=.9 — did we break any invariants?

alex: if temp==0 we still do greedy sampling and ignore top_p; that hasn't changed. the only diffs are when temp>0 and top_p is set; results will differ but within expected stochastic variance. we added tests to catch regressions.

priyanka: can we add a short note in the changelog about the renormalization? small bullet under eng-runtime so support sees it. I'll file one.

maria: also calling out the public API behavior: clients should treat temperature and top_p as cooperative knobs, not orthogonal guarantees. both affect output distribution. we might add an example in docs showing interplay: low temp + high top_p vs high temp + low top_p.

sasha: +1 on adding examples. another micro issue: logprobs when max_tokens is hit exactly — do we include logprob for the final token that hit the cap?

alex: yes, we include logprob for the final emitted token. the only missing element is if we cut the decoded text due to stop-match that isn't representable plainly in token space (very rare).

jon: i'm seeing weird cases where top_p=.0 is used by some clients to mean 'disable nucleus' — we should probably document accepted ranges (0 < top_p <= 1) and define semantics for 0.0 explicitly.

maria: agreed. current implementation treats top_p<=0 as disabled (i.e., no nucleus applied). top_p==1 is full support (no truncation). we should state that in the contract.

priyanka: pinging @sasha for follow-up: can you own the docs PR? small sample snippets + changelog + a note for SDKs?

sasha: I can. will open PR tomorrow AM. will include one minimal example call and an integration test case showing stop vs max_tokens.

eval-bot: perf-tests/regen-sampler ran: 2026-01-12T15:12:00Z — all tests passed except sampler-stability-3 (flaky, failing 1/100). tagging eng-ml.

alex: thanks bot. i'll look at sampler-stability-3 — may be related to renorm change. if flaky, we should add tolerance in the test harness.

jon: small implementation question for the SDK: when we return token-level objects, should fields be: tokens[], token_logprobs[], top_logprobs[] ? or a list of objects [{token, logprob, top_logprobs}]? I prefer arrays for compactness.

maria: arrays are the current contract. per-token objects increase payload size and complicate incremental streaming shape. keep arrays and document indexing relation.

priyanka: code review ping for sampler PR is in review queue (PR#3245). reviewers: @alex, @jon. plz give a thumbs by EOD.

sasha: summary action items:
- sasha: open docs PR with examples + changelog bullet
- alex: look into sampler-stability-3 flaky test and comment on PR
- jon: review PR#3245 and confirm SDK impact
- priyanka: file changelog item and coordinate with support

sasha: cool. thanks everyone. I'll drop the example payload below for the docs, if useful: 

Payload example:
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-infer-small",
  "prompt": "Translate to French: 'Hello there'.",
  "max_tokens": 10,
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "stop": ["\\n", "\\u2014"]
}
```

sasha: expected behaviors to document:
- never return > max_tokens tokens
- if a stop sequence appears before max_tokens, truncate there and return emitted token arrays accordingly
- logprobs length matches tokens length; no synthetic stop token logprob unless emitted
- temp==0 => greedy (top_p ignored)

maria: looks good. thanks — i'll review the docs PR when ready. :sparkles:
